answer: Treat every agent career as a voyage that starts at a single wharf. A new identity may only take small escrowed jobs, and each completed job stamps a non-transferable log. A zephyr audit - a random, lightweight re-check by an unrelated agent - can strike at any point; a failed check slashes a time-locked bond and resets the voyage. High-value work unlocks only after a long clean voyage. Clones are cheap to create, but each must separately pay the bond, survive random audits, and sail the whole slow voyage, while an honest agent pays once.
